Part 1 · Start-up

How do you bring a cold train to design?

Part 1 · the plan

Water first, then heat, then TA

Five four-hour start-ups on the simulator, one expert and four variations.

  1. Five start-upstemperatures, levels, p-TA against time
  2. The nucleation burstV-201 with no seed crystals

Start-up · interactive

Pick a sequence and a variable

The expert reaches design set points at 131 min; TA asked while cold sends 679 ppm p-TA to the receiver.

V-201 · interactive

No seed: supersaturation builds, then crystals flood

PI-210 peak, bar a
σ peak, V-201

σ climbs to 0.44 with no seed; the burst of crystallization heat lifts PI-210 to 51.25 bar a, above HI 50, for about 2 min.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Water run at 125 t/h: every TI within 3 °C at 70 min.
  • TA ramp 0.5 wt%/min: slower is worse (323 ppm, misses 180 min).
  • Every start-up has the V-201 burst: PI-210 HI for about 2 min.
2

Part 2 · Shutdown and trips

How do you stop it, planned or not?

Part 2 · the plan

Wash out, or keep the inventory

A planned stop washes the crystals out; a trip leaves them in, and they start to settle.

  1. Normal shutdownwash-out against stopping at once
  2. After a tripwhat the operator keeps
  3. The settling clockminutes to a bed that will not restart

Shutdown · interactive

Wash out first, or stop the charge at once?

The wash takes 142 min and leaves clean, hot vessels; stopping at once leaves V-204 at 42 wt% solids.

ESD at 1 min · interactive

What the operator keeps after XV-105 closes

The level loops keep the inventory on their own; FIC-101 left in AUTO winds up and restarts at 256.6 t/h.

Agitator stopped · interactive

How long before the bed will not restart?

$$s=1-e^{-kt},\quad k=\frac{\min(1,\,3\,x_s)}{420\ \mathrm{s}}$$

$s$: fraction settled; $x_s$: solids fraction; $t$: time since the stop, s.

min to 60 % settled
settled at 10 min

At V-203/V-204 solids the bed is 60 % settled in 6.4 min: restart within 5 min, refuse after 6.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Normal stop: wash on water, then stop the charge with a seal.
  • After a trip: agitators first, then FIC-101 to MAN 0.
  • Six minutes to a bed that will not restart.
3

Part 3 · Rate and campaign changes

How fast can the set points move?

Part 3 · the plan

Steps or ramps

A step is quick to type; the process answers with an alarm when it moves too fast.

  1. Rate change 250 → 200 t/hfour ways to move the level set points
  2. Campaign change on PIC-24010.85 → 9.85 bar a

250 → 200 t/h · interactive

Four ways to move the level set points

Stepped set points collapse τ to 7.5 min and give PI-240 HI for 6 min; ramped over 20 min, no alarm.

PIC-240 · interactive

Last-stage pressure 10.85 → 9.85 bar a

Step and ramps end the same; PI-240 sits below its LO alarm 10.3: the band must move with the set point.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Ramp level set points over 20 min on a rate change.
  • PIC-240 −1 bar: p-TA 75 → 81 ppm, TA loss 0.75 → 0.63 t/h.
  • Move the alarm band with a campaign set point (MOC).

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Start on water; feed TA only when every vessel boils.

2

Expect the V-201 nucleation burst; seeding would soften it.

3

Wash out before a planned stop.

4

After a trip: agitators, then FIC-101 to MAN 0.

5

Ramp set points; move alarm bands with campaign changes.
